details: CONFIRMED by a free probe of the installed eval tool (claude 2.1.310) on a scratch copy: with the expect: lines it refuses the case
with "Unrecognized key(s) in object: 'expect'" for every grader; the same copy with the expect: lines removed passes the schema
and stops at the next check ("execution.prompt is required"). Read in the tool's loader: ou(name, frontmatter, body) returns
{name, ...frontmatter, criteria: body}; the llm grader schema ends .strict(). No test loads the cases with the eval tool, so the
29 tally tests and make.py --check pass while the paid run is broken; it would show up only as a failed paid run (cost, time) or,
worse, a tally of a run where every case failed to load.
Size: 30 agent minutes (move the field to a sidecar file written by make.py, read it in load_answers, revert the 58 grader edits,
add the key test, probe the tool once).
evidence: x .../measure-off-by-one/case.yaml: invalid case.yaml:   graders.0: Unrecognized key(s) in object: 'expect'   graders.1: Unrecognized key(s) in object: 'expect' ...
x .../measure-off-by-one/case.yaml: execution.prompt is required (a prompt.md body, or execution.prompt in case.yaml)
binary strings: function ou(e,n,r){let a={name:e,...n},...a[s]=r;return a}
failing_case: The README's run command, `claude plugin eval . --eval-dir evals/judge-measure ...`, on this branch: the eval tool builds each
grader as {name, ...front matter, criteria: body} and checks it with a strict schema (llm: type, name, criteria, focus, weight,
arm). Now it prints "invalid case.yaml: graders.0: Unrecognized key(s) in object: 'expect' ..." for each case, "0 case(s)" and
"case file(s) failed to load". tally.py then answers NOT JUDGED "missing case". The owner can never measure a judge again.
It should load all four cases as on master, while tally.py still reads the stored expected answer.
fix_hint: Keep the grader files as on master and store the answers beside them, outside graders/ (the tool reads graders/ as graders):
make.py writes <case>/answers.json, {"<grader name>": "PASS"|"FAIL"} from items.txt, and checks it under --check; load_answers
reads that file; a grader missing from it stays NOT JUDGED. Add the front-matter key test, update README and the docstrings, and
probe one case with the eval tool as in pass-case 1.
pass_cases: 1. A scratch copy of measure-off-by-one, with its prompt.md body emptied so nothing runs: `claude plugin eval <copy> --case
measure-off-by-one --runs 1 --ablation none --no-publish --trust-plugin` reports "execution.prompt is required" (the case passed
the schema), not "Unrecognized key(s) ... 'expect'". Same for the other three cases.
2. A free test: every front-matter key of every evals/judge-measure/*/graders/*.md is one of type, focus, weight, arm (the keys the
eval tool accepts besides name and criteria), so a new key fails the test, not a paid run.
3. tally.py still reads the expected answer from a stored field, never the name: a grader named yes--01-a stored as FAIL, judged
F,F,F in 5 runs, gives exit 0 (test_the_stored_field_decides_not_the_name keeps passing).
4. A grader in the result with no stored answer exits 2 and names the grader; removing one stored answer from the committed files
makes load_answers (or its successor) raise NotJudged naming that grader.
5. make.py --check exits 0 and fails when the stored answer of one grader is changed by hand.
findings.summary: the new expect: key in every grader's front matter makes the eval tool refuse all four measure cases, so the measurement run loads 0 cases

details: CONFIRMED by reading main(): the try around json.load also holds load_expected() and load_answers(), whose OSError and
ValueError fall into "cannot read {a.json}". Correct exit code today, misleading message. Size: 5 agent minutes (load the
expected counts and answers before the try that reads the input, with their own message).
evidence: tally.py main(): try: open(a.json) / json.load / tally(..., load_expected(), load_answers()) except (OSError, ValueError): "cannot read {a.json}"
failing_case: A case folder without graders/ (or questions.json unreadable): os.listdir raises FileNotFoundError in load_answers, and the line
says "cannot read <eval.json>: [Errno 2] ... graders", blaming the result file. A KeyError from a bug in tally() reads
"<eval.json> does not have the shape of an eval result". Exit 2 is right; the cause named is wrong.
fix_hint: Call load_expected() and load_answers() before the input try, letting their NotJudged or OSError produce a message naming the eval folder.
pass_cases: 2. A copy of the eval folder with one graders/ directory removed: exit 2, one line that names that folder, not the --json file.
3. JSON of another shape still exits 2 with "does not have the shape of an eval result" (test_json_of_another_shape).
reason: tests/test_judge_tally.py ExpectedAnswerIsAField::test_a_broken_eval_folder_is_not_blamed_on_the_input_file passes, fails at 8e0799a; test_an_empty_file and test_json_of_another_shape pass.
findings.summary: main() wraps load_expected/load_answers and tally() in the input-error catch, so a broken eval folder or a tally bug is reported as an unreadable or misshapen input file
